title: Human-in-the-Loop & Safe Fallbacks
interviewAnswer: Human-in-the-loop is useful when errors are costly, uncertainty can be detected and a qualified reviewer can actually improve decisions. I define escalation thresholds, what context the human sees, and a safe fallback when the model or reviewer is unavailable.
why: Adding a human checkbox does not automatically make a system safe; poor alert quality can create automation bias or reviewer fatigue.
intuition: Use humans where judgment changes the outcome, not as decoration after the model already acted.
deepDive: Escalation can be based on confidence, novelty, policy category or consequence. Review interfaces should expose evidence and allow disagreement. Measure human+AI performance, not model performance alone.
workedExample: An engineering failure classifier can auto-handle obvious safe cases, escalate borderline/high-risk cases, and default to conservative behavior if inference is unavailable.
commonMistakes: Escalating so many cases that reviewers rubber-stamp them.
Assuming model confidence is perfectly calibrated.
followUps: How do you choose an escalation threshold?
production: Track queue size, override rate, reviewer agreement and post-review outcomes; overload needs a graceful conservative mode.

visual.title: Human-in-the-loop decision
visual.caption: Human review is most useful when routing rules are explicit and feedback returns to the system.
